papers.title: Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics
papers.authors: Ganesh Ananthanarayanan, Matthew Balkwill, Xenofon Foukas, Sanjeev Mehrotra, Bozidar Radunovic, Connor Settle, Ankit Verma, David White, Shawn Cicoria, Mark Martin, Rachel Johnson, Mayur Patel
papers.summary: Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads. papers.title: Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera
papers.authors: Felix Pultar, John Gardner, Guoqing Liu, Marwin Segler
papers.summary: Custom-made molecules are advancing medicine, materials, and agriculture, but producing them is slow and expensive. A new Nature paper highlights RetroChimera, a predictive model that helps accelerate chemical synthesis, helping researchers explore a wide range of molecules. papers.authors: Naoto Usuyama, Jeya Maria Jose Valanarasu, Tristan Naumann
papers.summary: What if pathology foundation models could do more with less? GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash cut computational demands while maintaining strong performance, opening the door to larger studies and broader exploration. papers.title: Orchard: An open framework for scalable agentic AI
papers.authors: Baolin Peng, Wenlin Yao, Qianhui Wu, Hao Cheng, Jianfeng Gao
papers.summary: Orchard is an open-source framework for the research community to train and evaluate AI agents across task types. It reduces complexity while supporting strong performance from smaller models by enabling researchers to reuse the same infrastructure. papers.title: Echoverse: Deep, evolving environments for computer-use agents
papers.authors: Akshay Nambi, Yash Pandya, Sahil Gupta, Sarthak Harne, Kavyansh Chourasia, Yash Lara, Ahmed Awadallah
papers.summary: Computer-use AI agents struggle with multi-step workflows like email and customer support. Echoverse trains agents in realistic environments rather than simply providing more training tasks, helping them improve as the tasks, tests, and environments evolve. papers.summary: LLMs do not get smarter just by remembering more. EvoLib turns experience into evolving knowledge, taking reusable skills and insights that help models learn and adapt across tasks long after deployment.
